systemic_findings: target_span.end is wrong on 3354/5386 rows (end != start+len(text)); starts are correct. Fix rule: end = start + len(text). Not itemised below.
4693/5386 rows use the whole message as the candidate span, so multi-clause messages are not sentence-split as the spec's splitter requires.
22 new_rule_spans entries are dicts, 603 are strings; writer should emit one shape (span objects with offsets).
16 rows carry the spec's own illustration pairs verbatim (both copies); one copy of each is dropped as a duplicate, the survivors stay development-only.
No benchmark echo found: lexical scan of old_rule+message for every excluded evaluation family named in LABELS-RELATIONS.md returned 0 hits. No sealed input and no file under data/bench was opened.
summary.main_relabel_class: 50 rows labelled supersedes against a cancelled/completed/superseded target (changed-value reinstatement). The corpus' own majority convention labels these none (+message_new_rule) on the inactive version and supersedes only on a live same-key version; the spec's status preconditions ('supersedes targets applicable/shadowable rules') agree.
ambiguities: Scoped skips ('for this release, skip the unit tests') are labelled supersedes throughout; defensible under overlap-scope wording, but D5 cut exception mechanics, so the spec does not say outright whether a scoped suspension is supersedes or none.
Hedged proposals ('I think we should switch to X') are sometimes supersedes, sometimes none; the spec's uncertainty carve-out has no strength threshold.
completes on a task whose message also preserves the rule globally (e.g. row 207) is annotated completes; the spec does not say whether the surviving global admission changes the pair label.
